name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: No polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Bost's incumbency and roughly 15-to-1 fundraising edge over Julie Fortier, and Polymarket pricing the Democrat at just 3% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. No polls or expert ratings justify moving from the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a major outside-spending influx for Fortier would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southern Illinois' 12th district leans heavily Republican, with a partisan advantage of about 22 points favoring the GOP. Incumbent Mike Bost is running for another term and holds a commanding financial edge, having raised over $1.3 million with roughly $790,000 on hand. Democrat Julie Fortier has raised under $90,000, and no outside spending has materialized on either side.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which price Bost's chances at about 96%. The expected margin is around 19 points for Bost, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
